accepted.s: Operation Chinnari-Thalli, launched by the Andhra Pradesh Police in February 2026, primarily targets which of the following?
accepted.x: Operation Chinnari-Thalli was launched by the Andhra Pradesh Police in February 2026 to target sexual offences against children.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme from its stated objective and implementing agency.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - child protection mechanisms and POCSO courts  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Operation Chinnari-Thalli?
o: Providing free coaching for competitive examinations
Achieving zero pendency in POCSO cases
accepted.x: Operation Chinnari-Thalli includes Sexual Offender Sheets, zero pendency in POCSO cases and chargesheets within 60 days. Free coaching for competitive examinations is not one of its stated features.
accepted.tq: Find the option unrelated to the programme’s stated functions.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - child protection mechanisms and POCSO courts  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The “Good touch-bad touch” awareness programme in schools and hostels in Andhra Pradesh is conducted by which wing?
accepted.x: The Women & Child Safety Wing conducts “Good touch-bad touch” awareness programmes in schools and hostels.
accepted.tq: Match the activity with the specialised administrative wing.
accepted.sec: Andhra Pradesh - child protection mechanisms and POCSO courts  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (ILO Convention)
 a. Convention No. 138

 ii. Minimum Age for Employment

accepted.s: In which year did India ratify both ILO Convention No. 138 and ILO Convention No. 182?
accepted.x: India ratified both ILO Convention No. 138 and Convention No. 182 in 2017.
accepted.tq: Use the year-specific numerical recall pattern.

accepted.s: Under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, a child is generally understood as a person below which age?
accepted.x: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child treats a child as a person below 18 years of age.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the international child-rights age threshold from domestic employment thresholds.
accepted.sec: ILO core conventions on child labour and India's ratification  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The World Day Against Child Labour is observed on:
accepted.x: The World Day Against Child Labour is observed on 12 June.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific international observance date.
accepted.sec: ILO core conventions on child labour and India's ratification  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to Census 2011, the number of child labourers in the 5–14 age group in India was approximately:
accepted.x: Census 2011 recorded approximately 10.1 million child labourers aged 5–14. The 4.35 million figure refers only to main workers.
accepted.tq: Separate the overall count from the narrower main-worker figure.
accepted.sec: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the gender-wise distribution of child labourers aged 5–14 according to Census 2011?
accepted.x: The Census 2011 count included approximately 5.6 million boys and 4.5 million girls.
accepted.tq: Compare the two component figures rather than relying only on the total.
accepted.sec: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the rural-urban distribution of child labour according to Census 2011 figures?
o: About 10 million urban and 1 million rural child labourers
About 5 million each in rural and urban areas
About 2 million rural and 8 million urban child labourers
About 8 million rural and 2 million urban child labourers
accepted.x: Approximately 8 million child labourers were in rural areas and 2 million were in urban areas. Urban child labour, however, was noted to be rising.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison between rural magnitude and urban trend.
accepted.sec: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The figure of 4.35 million in relation to child labour refers to:
o: Child labourers in urban areas only
accepted.x: The 4.35 million figure counts main workers only; it is not the total number of child labourers aged 5–14.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the total count and the narrower statistical category.
accepted.sec: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct descending sequence of the states identified among the leading states in child labour?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh
Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh
Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh
Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: The listed order is Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Preserve the sequence exactly when the question supplies a ranked list.
accepted.sec: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The fall in child labour from 2001 to 2011 was approximately:
accepted.x: The decline from 2001 to 2011 was only about 2.2% per year.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise trend figure instead of confusing it with the census totals.
accepted.sec: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following sectors are associated with child labour as identified in the given context?
1. Brick kilns
2. Pesticide-heavy farm work
3. Work involving toxic chemicals
4. Tea stalls
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Brick kilns, pesticide-heavy farm work, toxic chemicals and tea stalls are all identified sectors or settings associated with child labour.
accepted.tq: Include all sector examples and avoid narrowing the list to hazardous industrial work alone.
accepted.sec: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following figures correctly represents the global child labour situation in 2024?
o: 10.1 million, including 4.35 million in hazardous work
54 million, including 137.6 million in hazardous work
137.6 million, including 54 million in hazardous work
accepted.x: The global figure for 2024 was 137.6 million child labourers, of whom 54 million were in hazardous work.
accepted.tq: Match the total and the sub-category without reversing their relationship.
accepted.sec: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: How many children did India rescue from child labour during 2024-25, according to the cited figure?
accepted.x: India rescued more than 40,000 children from child labour during 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the national rescue figure from the programme-specific figures.
accepted.sec: Magnitude - Census 2011 count, top states, sectors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a cause or contributing factor of child labour?
accepted.x: Poverty, debt bondage and weak enforcement are identified causes. Universal access to quality education is not a cause of child labour.
accepted.tq: Find the positive protective condition among the listed causal factors.
accepted.sec: Causes - poverty, illiteracy, debt bondage, migrant families, cheap labour  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Why do employers often prefer child labour, according to the stated economic explanation?
o: Children can independently negotiate employment contracts
Children are legally entitled to higher wages
Children provide more work for less pay
accepted.x: Employers may obtain more work for less pay by employing children, creating an economic incentive for child labour.
accepted.tq: Apply the cause-effect relationship to the employer’s incentive.
accepted.sec: Causes - poverty, illiteracy, debt bondage, migrant families, cheap labour  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was NOT listed among the additional causes of child labour?
1. Family disorganisation
2. Lack of awareness
3. Kidnapping
4. Weak enforcement
5. Universal adult literacy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Family disorganisation, lack of awareness, kidnapping and weak enforcement were listed causes. Universal adult literacy was not listed as a cause.
accepted.tq: Locate the single inserted factor that does not belong to the causal list.
accepted.sec: Causes - poverty, illiteracy, debt bondage, migrant families, cheap labour  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Debt bondage is associated with child and bonded labour particularly in which of the following settings?
1. Farms
2. Brick kilns
3. Domestic work
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Debt bondage drives child and bonded labour in farms, brick kilns and domestic work.
accepted.tq: Test whether all the sectoral examples in the causal statement are retained.
accepted.sec: Causes - poverty, illiteracy, debt bondage, migrant families, cheap labour  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The abolition of bonded labour is specifically associated with which law?
accepted.x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 outlawed bonded labour.
accepted.tq: Match the social evil with the legislation that abolished it.
accepted.sec: Causes - poverty, illiteracy, debt bondage, migrant families, cheap labour  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Twenty-nine Chenchu and Yanadi tribal persons from Prakasam were rescued from a coal kiln in which State?
accepted.x: Twenty-nine Chenchu and Yanadi tribals from Prakasam were rescued from a coal kiln in Telangana.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the source district and the location of rescue.
accepted.sec: Causes - poverty, illiteracy, debt bondage, migrant families, cheap labour  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which constitutional provision directs that the tender age of children should not be abused and that citizens should not be forced by economic necessity into work unsuited to their age or strength?
accepted.x: Article 39(e), a Directive Principle of State Policy, addresses protection of tender age and work unsuitable to age or strength.
accepted.tq: Match the specific constitutional language with the correct Article.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 24, 39(e), 39(f), 21A  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Article 39(f) seeks to ensure that children:
o: Are employed in all non-hazardous occupations
Are denied education until the age of 18
Develop in freedom and dignity and are protected against exploitation
accepted.x: Article 39(f) provides for children to develop in freedom and dignity and for childhood and youth to be protected against exploitation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two child-protection principles under Article 39 from employment prohibitions.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 24, 39(e), 39(f), 21A  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the constitutional provision with its nature?
o: Article 24 — Directive Principle of State Policy
Article 39(f) — Directive Principle of State Policy
Article 21A — Directive Principle of State Policy
accepted.x: Article 39(f) is a Directive Principle of State Policy. Articles 24 and 21A are Fundamental Rights, while Article 39(e) is also a Directive Principle.
accepted.tq: Use the Fundamental Right–DPSP distinction to eliminate swapped classifications.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 24, 39(e), 39(f), 21A  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the age limits under the Factories Act, 1948 and the Mines Act, 1952?
o: Factories Act: below 14 prohibited; Mines Act: below 16 prohibited
Factories Act: below 18 prohibited; Mines Act: below 14 prohibited
Factories Act: below 14 prohibited; Mines Act: below 18 prohibited
Factories Act: below 16 prohibited; Mines Act: below 18 prohibited
accepted.x: The Factories Act, 1948 prohibits employment of children below 14, while the Mines Act, 1952 prohibits anyone below 18 from working in mines.
accepted.tq: Compare the two age thresholds without interchanging the Acts.
accepted.sec: Factories Act and Mines Act age limits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, working children are treated as:
o: Adult workers requiring wage protection only
Children in conflict with law in every case
Children in need of care and protection
accepted.x: The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 treats working children as children in need of care and protection.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct statutory child-protection category.
accepted.sec: Factories Act and Mines Act age limits  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A Private Member’s Bill reported in December 2025 sought to lower the heinous-offence threshold under the juvenile justice framework from:
accepted.x: The Bill sought to lower the heinous-offence threshold from 16 years to 14 years.
accepted.tq: Track the direction and magnitude of the proposed age change.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The parliamentary standing committee on home affairs had earlier recommended lowering the juvenile age from:
accepted.x: The committee had earlier recommended lowering the juvenile age from 18 years to 16 years.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the committee’s earlier recommendation from the later Private Member’s Bill.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following criticisms is associated with the transfer system and POCSO?
o: The transfer system may erode rehabilitation, while POCSO may criminalise consensual adolescent relationships.
The transfer system eliminates rehabilitation and POCSO excludes all minors from protection.
The transfer system applies only to adults and POCSO concerns only labour disputes.
Neither issue has been raised in public debate.
accepted.x: The cited criticisms are that the transfer system can erode rehabilitation and that POCSO can criminalise consensual adolescent relationships.
accepted.tq: Select the option that accurately combines two related criticisms without using absolute language.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Andhra Pradesh child-protection framework and Mission Vatsalya?
o: The framework follows only the Factories Act; Mission Vatsalya funds only urban schools.
The framework follows the JJ Act 2015 and Probation of Offenders Act 1958; Mission Vatsalya funds JJBs and CWCs in every district.
The framework excludes the JJ Act and supports only private adoption agencies.
The framework follows the Mines Act; Mission Vatsalya funds only police stations.
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh framework follows the JJ Act 2015 and the Probation of Offenders Act 1958. Mission Vatsalya funds Juvenile Justice Boards and Child Welfare Committees in every district.
accepted.tq: Link the legal framework with the institutions supported by the scheme.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Mission Vatsalya was implemented during which period with an outlay and funding ratio stated as follows?
accepted.x: Mission Vatsalya covers 2021-22 to 2025-26, has an outlay of Rs 10,916 crore and follows a 60:40 funding ratio.
accepted.tq: Check the period, financial amount and sharing ratio as a combined numerical set.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In State of U.P. v. Anurudh, the Supreme Court urged consideration of which approach in relation to consensual adolescent relationships?
o: A complete repeal of the Juvenile Justice Act
A blanket exclusion of all minors from POCSO
accepted.x: In State of U.P. v. Anurudh, the Supreme Court flagged misuse of POCSO in consensual adolescent relationships and urged a “Romeo-Juliet” clause.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive judicial phrase associated with the case.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding consensual adolescent relationships and POCSO:
1. The Supreme Court held that a minor cannot consent.
2. The Supreme Court set aside a Calcutta High Court ruling that had kept consensual adolescent relationships outside POCSO.
3. The Supreme Court used Article 142 to allow flexibility in sentencing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Supreme Court held that a minor cannot consent, set aside the Calcutta High Court ruling and invoked Article 142 for sentencing flexibility.
accepted.tq: Test the holding, the appellate action and the constitutional power together.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In a custody dispute involving a child alleged to be an abuse victim, the Supreme Court emphasised that child assessments should involve:
accepted.x: The Supreme Court stated that assessments of such children should involve minimum intrusion.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise judicial standard rather than an exaggerated alternative.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares the United Kingdom’s proposed social-media restriction with India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023?
o: The UK will ban social media for under-16s from spring 2027, while India requires verifiable parental consent below 18 under Section 9.
The UK will ban social media for under-18s from 2026, while India requires consent below 16 under Section 21.
India has no provision concerning parental consent for children.
Both countries prohibit social media access below 14 without exception.
accepted.x: The UK proposal concerns under-16s from spring 2027. Section 9 of India’s DPDP Act, 2023 requires verifiable parental consent for persons below 18.
accepted.tq: Keep the two jurisdictions, age thresholds and legal provisions separate.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which pair correctly represents the two policy options discussed in the debate over consensual adolescent relationships?
o: Close-in-age exemption; or retaining the age of consent at 18 with judicial discretion
Replacing POCSO with the Mines Act; or removing judicial review
Abolition of the age of consent; or compulsory imprisonment in every case
Lowering the age of consent to 12; or excluding all adolescents from POCSO
accepted.x: The two options discussed are a close-in-age exemption or retaining the age of consent at 18 while allowing judicial discretion.
accepted.tq: Identify the balanced alternatives rather than absolute positions.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the reported trends in POCSO-related case outcomes?
o: Disposals increased by 109%, while convictions were falling.
Disposals fell by 109%, while convictions were rising.
Both disposals and convictions increased by 109%.
Both disposals and convictions were unchanged.
accepted.x: The reported trend was that disposals increased by 109%, whereas convictions were falling.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the two opposing trends in the comparison.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: An NCPCR campaign reported rescuing more than how many children from child labour and sought State data on FIRs, rehabilitation and school mainstreaming?
accepted.x: The NCPCR campaign rescued more than 3,800 children and sought State data on FIRs, rehabilitation and school mainstreaming.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the NCPCR campaign figure from other rescue totals.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the Andhra Pradesh figures for 2024-25?
o: 342 street children rescued and 877 child marriages prevented
3,800 street children rescued and 1,200 child marriages prevented
877 street children rescued and 342 child marriages prevented
1,200 street children rescued and 3,800 child marriages prevented
accepted.x: APSES 2024-25 recorded 342 street children rescued and 877 child marriages prevented.
accepted.tq: Keep the two activity figures matched with their respective outcomes.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which organisation conducted the “Back to School” drive in Guntur?
accepted.x: DLSA Guntur conducted the “Back to School” drive.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementing body from the programme name and location.
